Jerimoth
jer'i-moth
n. (a name borne by several Levites, singers and captains, including one of the fourteen sons of Heman and an overseer under Hezekiah)
From Hebrew Yerimoth, from rum, to be high — “elevations” or “heights”. Chronicles also spells it Jeremoth, and both forms stand in the KJV for the same name.

Biblical Definition

Jerimoth runs through the Chronicler's lists of the men who organized Israel's worship. He is a son of Mushi in the Merarite courses — “The sons also of Mushi; Mahli, and Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after the house of their fathers” (1Ch 24:30). He is one of the fourteen sons of Heman the king's seer, all of them appointed to the ministry of song: “the sons of Heman; Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth…” (1Ch 25:4), and the lot for the fifteenth course fell to him with twelve of his sons and brethren (1Ch 25:22). Under Hezekiah, when the temple was cleansed and the people brought in tithes and offerings in such heaps that store chambers had to be prepared, a Jerimoth is one of the ten men appointed to manage them: “overseers under the hand of Cononiah and Shimei his brother, at the commandment of Hezekiah the king” (2Ch 31:13). Singing, and then counting what the singing brought in. The Chronicler is interested in both, and never treats the second as beneath the first.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Jerimoth; in sacred history it is the name of several Levites and captains, including a son of Heman among the temple singers.

expand to see more

JERIMOTH, n. The name signifies heights or elevations; written also Jeremoth.

A son of Mushi, in the courses of the Levites appointed by David.

One of the fourteen sons of Heman, set apart to prophesy with harps and psalteries.

The fifteenth lot of the singers came forth to Jerimoth, with twelve of his sons and brethren.

An overseer of the tithes and dedicated things in the reign of Hezekiah bore the same name.

Key Scripture

1Ch 24:30 — "The sons also of Mushi; Mahli, and Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites after the house of their fathers."

1Ch 25:4 — "Of Heman: the sons of Heman; Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, and Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, and Romamtiezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth:"

2Ch 31:13 — "And Jehiel, and Azaziah, and Nahath, and Asahel, and Jerimoth, and Jozabad, and Eliel, and Ismachiah, and Mahath, and Benaiah, were overseers under the hand of Cononiah and Shimei his brother, at the commandment of Hezekiah the king, and Azariah the ruler of the house of God."

1Ch 6:20 — "Of Gershom; Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,"

Modern Corruption

The ordered, appointed, rota-governed worship of Chronicles is dismissed as dead formalism, and the singers' ministry reduced to entertainment; Scripture treats both the order and the song as commanded service.

expand to see more

Chronicles devotes chapters to who sang, when, with what instrument, and in what order, and the modern reader is inclined to hear only bureaucracy. That is a failure of imagination about what worship is. David appointed the singers by lot, so that the humblest course had the same title to its week as the greatest, and the whole arrangement was “according to the order of the king” — itself given, Chronicles says elsewhere, by the commandment of the LORD by His prophets (2Ch 29:25). Order in worship is not the enemy of life in worship; it is the form life takes when it is offered to a God who is not mocked. The regulative principle stands on exactly this ground: God says how He will be approached.

The second corruption is the modern reduction of church music to a means of producing feeling. The Chronicler will not have it. These men are said to prophesy with harps, psalteries and cymbals; their business was the word of God set to music and sung back to Him. Paul keeps the same standard: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs” (Col 3:16). Singing is teaching. A congregation is catechized by what it sings far more thoroughly than by what it hears preached, which is why the content of the songs is a matter of doctrine and not of taste.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Yerimoth (H3406), Jerimoth; rum (H7311), to be high, exalted; naba' (H5012), to prophesy; goral (H1486), lot; maqhelah, choir, assembly.

expand to see more

Hebrew Yerimoth (H3406) — Jerimoth; heights, elevations; written also Jeremoth.

Hebrew rum (H7311) — to be high, rise, be exalted; the root of the name.

Hebrew naba' (H5012) — to prophesy; Chronicles' verb for the ministry of the singers.

Hebrew goral (H1486) — lot; how the twenty-four courses were assigned.

Hebrew ma'aser (H4643) — tithe; what the Hezekiah-era Jerimoth was set over.

Usage

"“The fifteenth to Jeremoth, he, his sons, and his brethren” — a course assigned by lot."

"“The sons of Heman… and Jerimoth” — fourteen sons, all of them singers."

"“Were overseers… at the commandment of Hezekiah the king” — the singer set over the stores."
